recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一個巨噬細胞內塞滿大量大小一致、約 2–4 µm 的卵圓形酵母菌，每個周圍有透明暈圈，一端可見新月形深染核質，無動基體（kinetoplast），符合莢膜組織漿菌（Histoplasma capsulatum）。
features: Macrophage distended by numerous small, uniform oval yeast forms (about 2–4 µm)
Each yeast with a clear halo (pseudocapsule) and a crescent-shaped basophilic nuclear cap at one pole
No kinetoplast, septation or budding with broad base identified
Occasional yeast forms also within an adjacent vacuolated macrophage
Background marrow cells including erythroid precursors and myeloid cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate shows a macrophage packed with numerous small, uniform oval intracellular yeasts measuring approximately 2–4 µm, each surrounded by a clear halo and containing an eccentric crescent of basophilic nuclear material. No kinetoplasts are identified. Similar organisms are seen in an adjacent vacuolated macrophage. In an immunocompromised patient with untreated HIV, findings are consistent with disseminated histoplasmosis; confirmation by GMS/PAS stain, culture and Histoplasma urine antigen is recommended.

ddx.vs: Leishmania amastigotes have both a nucleus and a rod-shaped kinetoplast and lack a clear halo, and are GMS negative.
Talaromyces yeasts divide by fission with a central transverse septum and include elongated sausage forms.
Toxoplasma tachyzoites are crescent-shaped with a central nucleus, lack a halo and are GMS negative.
Cryptococcus is larger and more variable in size (4–10 µm) with a thick mucicarmine-positive capsule and narrow-based budding.
